headline: 200+ masked men raze Mirpur healthcare center with bulldozers
summary: The Radda MCH-FP Center was demolished by a mob of 200 masked attackers, leading to a police negligence probe and the arrest of four suspects.
details: Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur-1, taking security guards hostage and looting medicines, vaccines, and equipment.

The attackers used heavy machinery to demolish one permanent building and three semi-permanent structures, completely leveling the facility that provided essential child health and family planning services.
DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan has demanded a fair and impartial investigation, stating that political or social influence should not protect the perpetrators or the masterminds.
The facility's management filed a case at Shah Ali police station, alleging that a certain group had been attempting to occupy the land for a long time.
The DMP Commissioner has ordered a probe into police negligence, investigating why the demolition occurred overnight without intervention.
Four suspects have already been arrested and sent to jail in connection with the attack and vandalism.
The center was a vital resource for Mirpur residents, offering vaccinations and reproductive health services to children and mothers.
caption:
200 masked men and bulldozers leveled a vital healthcare center in Mirpur overnight. Who was behind it?

Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur-1, taking security guards hostage and looting medicines, vaccines, and equipment.

The attackers used heavy machinery to demolish one permanent building and three semi-permanent structures, completely leveling the facility that provided essential child health and family planning services.

DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan has demanded a fair and impartial investigation, stating that political or social influence should not protect the perpetrators or the masterminds.

The facility's management filed a case at Shah Ali police station, alleging that a certain group had been attempting to occupy the land for a long time.

The DMP Commissioner has ordered a probe into police negligence, investigating why the demolition occurred overnight without intervention.

Four suspects have already been arrested and sent to jail in connection with the attack and vandalism.

The center was a vital resource for Mirpur residents, offering vaccinations and reproductive health services to children and mothers.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #Mirpur #HealthcareAttack #CrimeNews

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: Police raid JaSaD office in Dhaka, [[detain nearly 300 people]]
headline: Police raid JaSaD office in Dhaka, detain nearly 300 people
summary: Authorities apprehended 289 individuals from the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) headquarters in Gulistan, Dhaka. Police stated that JaSaD members will be released after verification.
details: Police conducted an operation at the central office of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) in Gulistan, Dhaka, detaining 289 people. According to police, JaSaD leaders and activists will be released after verification, while others will face legal action.

The raid, which began around 3 PM on Saturday, saw journalists, leaders, and activists apprehended and taken to the police station. Assistant Commissioner of DMP's Motijheel region, Shakibul Alam Bhuiyan, confirmed the detentions late Saturday night.

Earlier, police had stated the operation was based on information that members of the Awami League and its affiliated organizations had gathered at the JaSaD office, with 'Joy Bangla' slogans reportedly heard inside. However, JaSaD has denied these claims.

In a statement, JaSaD asserted that the meeting was a pre-scheduled central representative meeting, for which the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner, Motijheel DC, and Polton Police Station OC were informed. The party emphasized that it is not a banned organization and its activities are not restricted.

JaSaD claimed that approximately 500 of their leaders and activists, including 30 women, were present at the meeting. They alleged that members of Jubo Dal infiltrated the office amidst police presence, created a mob, and physically assaulted attendees before the police surrounded the premises.

The party's office secretary, Sajjad Hossain, mentioned that the former president of Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ), Abu Jafar Surya, was among those detained, stating he was present as a supporter of JaSaD.
